daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Attorney General's Office named Andri Mulyono as the fifth suspect in the Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) corruption case, detaining him at Salemba detention center for his role as a motor listrik supplier. Prosecutors revealed that Andri's company became a vendor despite lacking qualifications, and he marked up electric motorcycle prices while receiving 100 percent payment. The Attorney General's Office is also examining 26 prominent names provided by suspect Sony Sonjaya, who has requested to become a justice collaborator.

  • Home Affairs Minister Tito Karnavian urged regional governments to hold World Cup public viewing events to stimulate the economy.
  • A DPR member called on the government to thoroughly investigate the mafia involved in fraudulent hajj pilgrimage arrangements and illegal pilgrim deposits.
  • Minister Tito also pushed the election ethics council DKPP to strengthen integrity among election administrators as part of preventive measures.
  • Commission I of the DPR encouraged the strengthening of territorial duties for the Korem 081/DSJ Madiun military command.
  • The TNI confirmed that its personnel deployment during demonstrations in central Jakarta was at the request of the police, following student surprise at military presence at protests.
  • West Java prosecutors rescheduled the examination of Indramayu deputy regent who is a suspect in a corruption case involving DPR allowances.
  • Police claimed that certain groups attempted to hijack student demonstrations held on Thursday, which saw BEM UI protesters demand lower fuel prices and a halt to the MBG programme.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo held a phone call with the Dutch Prime Minister to discuss economic partnership and the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, amid heightened tensions in the region. The conversation comes as global energy security concerns mount following incidents in the strategic waterway. Indonesia is monitoring developments closely given its trade interests and reliance on stable maritime routes.

  • The Indonesian border management agency BNPP and Malaka district discussed establishing a free trade zone with Timor Leste along their shared border.
  • Indonesia and Australia strengthened cooperation in research and higher education sectors.
  • Indonesia will host an international women police conference in Bali.
  • Indonesia and Romania are seeking deeper cooperation in science and innovation.
  • The German President will visit Indonesia on June 15, with the German ambassador noting that the IEU-CEPA trade agreement has broad support in Europe.

Other

Bank Indonesia recorded US$1.06 billion in foreign capital inflows following its recent interest rate hike, providing a boost to market confidence amid currency pressures. The central bank's monetary tightening appears to be achieving its intended effect of attracting investment flows. Separately, Indonesia and China's central banks strengthened cooperation to bolster mutual economic stability.

  • A corruption case involving customs officials revealed that funds flowed to officials at BPOM and the Trade Ministry, with the defendant John Field expressing deep regret for paying billions in bribes.
  • Indonesia is investigating an illegal cigarette smuggling network amid efforts to combat illicit trade.
  • Authorities foiled the illegal trade of 100 endemic Papuan animals, part of efforts to protect endangered species.
  • Indonesia and China discussed cooperation potential in AI and the digital economy.
  • Danantara confirmed that the government is bankrolling the village cooperatives programme, which economists say must meet four requirements before supplying the free nutritious meals program.
